doc.title: Steve Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 25, 2002

title: Eddie Harris records, Excursions and the fan club
summary: Harris's trombone-mouthpiece tenor, his talking record and the group of Harris fans.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Yeah. They just re-released this record. It was one of the first records I was into after “Swiss Movement” was a record called “Excursions.” And it was a two record set which came out in I think 1973 or ’74. And it was a compilation of different sessions. Some of the things hadn’t been released and on one of those tunes he’s playing “Oleo.” I don’t remember who the band is right now but in the middle of the solo he plays a cappella and with the trombone mouthpiece on his tenor. I mean, amazing. And not just as a gimmick, but he really developed all this stuff. He was an amazing musician. And the language, he had his own language, the language he developed. Also on this record, I played for one of my students recently “Love For Sale” which is on this record. And to do what he does on that tune, you know, these fourth things, playing the tune, nobody was thinking about that when he did that. So to me Eddie is one of the great innovators, one of the great unsung geniuses man. We were listening on the way up here in the car I have a tape, an Eddie Harris record of him just talking, live in performances. I don’t know if I can say the title, I don’t know —
Okay. “Eddie Harris Talking Shit.” That’s what it’s called. And he’s just going on and on talking about different things to the audience. But he was a true original, a true original man.
Yeah he didn’t seem to care — didn’t he have an album called “I Need the Money.”
“I Need Some Money.” You know it’s like you just put it out there.

Yeah. You know I never got to meet him personally, unfortunately. Because there’s a small group of us who were big Eddie Harris fans. David Hazeltine, the great pianist, he played with Eddie for a bit. Johnny King is another great pianist. He’s another Eddie Harris fan. And a young tenor player by the name of Mark Turner. There’s a Eddie Harris fan club, we all get together and talk about it. Yeah, I just can’t say enough about it man. Just a true genius. Could play anything. Could play anything. And master of altissimo long before some of the guys we think about now, but just a true master of it. Yeah.
